text:
lina: hi team, first day stuff  accepted the org invite and added my SSH key, but git push keeps asking for credentials and then failing with a 403. I thought SSH would just work. any pointers? cc @ops

ops: welcome! can you paste `ssh -T git@github.com` output and the git remote url? also which SSH key did you add (work vs personal)?

lina: remote is `git@github.com:redwood-inference/app.git`. `ssh -T` gives: 
```
Warning: Permanently added the RSA host key for IP address '140.82.112.4' to the list of known hosts.
Hi lina-personal! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access.
```
which looks like it's using my personal key (`lina-personal`). I uploaded `~/.ssh/id_rsa` which I normally use for personal projects.

it-support: that explains it. Your personal key is tied to a different GH account (lina-personal) which doesn't have org access. Two approaches: 1) add a second key for your work account and name it `id_ed25519_work` and point your repo to use it via SSH config, OR 2) replace the key on your machine to the work key and re-upload. We also sometimes see credential helper fallbacks to HTTPS credentials if remote is `https://`. Any chance your local git is using an https remote for other clones?

lina: this repo was SSH. I don't have a work key yet. Can you outline the SSH config trick?

it-support: add a key and then in `~/.ssh/config`:
```
Host github-work
  HostName github.com
  User git
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work
  IdentitiesOnly yes
```
then set the repo remote to `git@github-work:redwood-inference/app.git` (note the host alias). That way your work key is used without replacing personal keys. After adding the work key to your work GH account, `ssh -T git@github-work` should show `Hi lina-work!`

lina: thanks, created the work key and added it to my work account. updated ssh config and remote. Now `ssh -T git@github-work` shows `Hi lina-work!`

ops: one more gotcha: org SSO enforcement requires the account to have the org-managed email verified. If your work GH account doesn't have the company email verified, SSO can still block access to some private repos even with membership. Check Settings -> Emails on your work account.

lina: checked and I had my personal email as primary. I added and verified my company email and re-run SSO. The push still failed once with 403 but then worked after I cleared the credential helper cache with `git credential-cache exit` and retried.

security-bot: Reminder: company policy requires using a device-bound SSH key or protected keyfile (no plain password-protected keys on shared machines). See onboarding docs for acceptable key types.

it-support: great, marking resolved. Summarized steps for the onboarding doc: 1) always create a dedicated work SSH key, 2) use SSH host alias to avoid clobbering personal keys, 3) verify org-managed email for SSO, 4) clear credential helpers if mixing HTTPS auth tokens.

lina: all good now, pushed my first commit :party_parrot:. thanks!

it-support: thread closed — resolved. :white_check_mark:
